observations: StrictMode mount/replay performs no search, save, or focus commands.
Reordering keyed editors preserves draft state, canonical frames, and endpoint identity.
Batched focus requests cancel the superseded revision and focus only the committed control.
Every accepted search launches despite batching; explicit request matching rejects an older result.
Reinserting a removed key creates fresh state while surviving siblings retain theirs.
Two accepted saves launch twice, and StrictMode replay never duplicates either command.
A service failure returns through a typed result and explicit status matching.
Removed owner cancellation and retained endpoint rejection prevent late work entering a replacement with the same key.
A synchronous completion waits until the transition's presentation effect launches; completion reduction never nests inside a phase.
Invalid presentation and duplicate child keys roll back state, ownership, and effect launch together.
Root teardown retires its subtree; adapter cleanup replay does not resurrect an owner.
The standalone demonstration searches and saves through actual HTTP responses from its foreground sample service, without request interception.
